articles.title: My mother donated her body to science. I really wasn’t prepared for what came next
articles.summary: The process included a gala featuring medical students doing aerial yoga and singing Taylor Swift to donors’ families. In some way, it was absolutely perfect. When my mother, Erin O’Connell, was diagnosed with a rare and aggressive cancer in late 2022, one of her first thoughts was: “What will I do…
body: At the time, she was 62 years old and working as a physical therapist in Portland, Oregon, where she had recently moved to live closer to me and my family. Reluctantly, she filed for short-term disability from her job and paused her training to become a volunteer search and rescue EMT.

My mom was 40 when she started physical therapy school. I was already a teenager. Despite her newfound stress, I remember how deeply it affected me to watch her fall in love with her work. The year she took anatomy lab she told my sister and me – and anyone who would listen – that dissecting a real human body was the coolest thing she had ever gotten to do, and when she died, she wanted to donate her body to science, too.
I spent so much of my childhood wanting nothing more than my mother’s hard-earned approval, and here she was, utterly devoted to a dead body. On some level, I was jealous of that cadaver.

articles.title: Attention LaMelo Ball: only losers boast about avoiding diaper duty | Arwa Mahdawi
articles.summary: The basketball star seems proud to leave the job to his partner. That’s so last century. Nobody can accuse the basketball star LaMelo Ball of being bad at his job. That said, the Minnesota Timberwolves point guard doesn’t seem to be a huge fan of dribbling.
body: Ball has a nine-month-old son, LaOne, with his partner Ana Montana (real name: Analicia Chaves) and is apparently uninterested in dealing with all the body fluids that come with a baby.
“You’re a dad now,” the sportscaster Ernie Johnson Jr said to Ball during an ESPN interview on Wednesday. “Are you a diaper changer?”
“Nah, my girl do all that,” Ball replied. “We got a good gameplan going on. So I know what I gotta do, bring to the table, she know what she gotta do, bring to the table.”
Johnson, to his credit, seemed disappointed by this answer. “Oh man, you don’t know what you’re missing, I’m telling you that.”

articles.title: The datacentre next door: on the frontline of tech’s latest David v Goliath battle
articles.summary: The AI boom is pitting local residents against corporate giants seeking to power their energy-hungry networks – but one Welsh city is fighting back. Dale Johnston opens the gate to his neat suburban garden on the western fringes of Newport in South Wales.
body: The 23 metre-high grey hulk looming over him and his neighbours is a hyperscale datacentre. It is heralded by the area’s Labour politicians as a job creator, yet all Johnston can think about is what he has lost: “Before, the sun used to come around here and it was lovely.” The way residents have been treated is “disgusting”.

Johnston can talk about little else, but he feels no one in authority is listening. He’s invited councillors and MPs backing the development to visit his garden. But “they won’t come around here to see what they’ve done”.

This is the frontline of Britain’s datacentre boom, which is pitting residents against giant US tech firms seeking to build a network of facilities capable of providing the immense computing muscle for powerful AI models. There are 315 hyperscale datacentres waiting to connect to the national grid, which carries electricity from power plants to homes and businesses (hyperscale typically means facilities with at least 5,000 servers and 10,000 sq ft in size). Combined, these new centres will require 73GW of power, 28GW higher than the typical peak energy demand of 45GW on a cold winter’s day.
points: The AI boom is pitting local residents against corporate giants seeking to power their energy-hungry networks – but one Welsh city is fighting back.

articles.title: How To Achieve the Soft, Plump Look of “Mochi Skin”
articles.summary: The "mochi skin" trend takes its name from the traditional Japanese rice cake treat famous for its bouncy texture, plump appearance, and smooth surface.
body: Beauty trends are constantly evolving, and this year clearly favors a more textured and luminous complexion—one that isn’t excessively shiny. On red carpets and social media alike, celebs and trendsetters seem to be moving away from ultra-glowy, glazed donut finishes in favor of skin that retains its texture, depth, and natural glow.

In other words, move over glass skin —right now, it’s all about “mochi skin.” This latest obsession from Japan focuses on a plump, fresh finish, one that calls to mind the softness and suppleness of the famous Japanese dessert for which it is named.

As mentioned, this new skin trend takes its name from mochi, a traditional Japanese rice cake treat famous for its bouncy texture, plump appearance, and smooth, slightly translucent surface. It’s easy to see how those descriptors would translate into an appealing skin look—after all, who among us doesn’t want “plump” “bouncy” and “smooth” skin? When it comes to mochi skin, the idea is to create an almost indulgent-looking complexion—one that appears as soft, smooth, and delicately plump as a delicious mochi treat.
points: The "mochi skin" trend takes its name from the traditional Japanese rice cake treat famous for its bouncy texture, plump appearance, and smooth surface.

articles.title: I Asked 8 Chefs to Name the Best Jarred Pasta Sauce — This Is the One They Swear By
articles.summary: Pasta is one of my favorite foods, and what really makes it is the sauce. A good sauce can often require simmering the ingredients for hours until all the flavors have melded. But sometimes we don’t have time for that.
body: So when we need something simple, quick, and easy to grab, jarred sauces can be a kitchen hero. I’ve tried many on the market, but was curious to learn which ones professional chefs give the stamp of approval. So I asked 8 chefs: What is the best jarred marinara sauce? One clearly swept the board but there were a few other favorites. Here are the jarred sauces you should stock your pantry shelves with.

The majority of the chefs (6 out of 8!) chose Rao’s Homemade as their top pick, praising it for being a great base for dishes like chicken Parmesan, lasagna, pasta puttanesca, and more. (It is Ina Garten’s favorite, too.) Jamie Milne, cookbook author of Everything Delish and busy mom of two, loves how close to homemade it tastes. “Rao’s has that rich, slow-simmered tomato flavor that you would expect from a sauce that’s been cooking on the stove for hours,” Milne said. “It’s made with simple ingredients like Italian tomatoes, olive oil, garlic, onions, and herbs, and you can really taste the difference.”

articles.title: This Joan Crawford Classic Still Has Something to Teach Us About Women—and the Clothes They Wear
articles.summary: The 1939 hit The Women spawned fashion trends, resurrected careers, launched new ones, and has fallen in and out of favor. Now, it’s enjoying another reconsideration, thanks to a new book by actress-turned-film scholar Illeana Douglas.
body: Growing up, Illeana Douglas spent a lot of time with her Oscar-winning grandfather in his Upper West Side apartment, where, salon-style, he would regularly host writers like Gore Vidal and screen legends like Myrna Loy. That duality seemed to inform the adult Illeana’s interests. In her twenties, she performed in a sketch comedy group at night, while holding down a day job as a film publicist, working on campaigns for future classics like The Princess Bride, The Untouchables, and Moonstruck.

She entered the ‘90s as one of Hollywood’s most reliable character actresses, stealing scenes in zeitgeist-defining films like Goodfellas and To Die For. “I would always get the part where I'd look through the script, and I’d go, ‘I don’t see any lines here,’” she says. “And they’d say, ‘Well, you'll come up with something brilliant’... So it was writing—but not realizing I was writing.”

articles.title: Baked Apple Cinnamon French Toast
articles.summary: As a working mom of two, I love a breakfast that feels special without requiring me to spend all morning in the kitchen. This baked apple cinnamon French toast is everything I want in a cozy breakfast: buttery, custardy, sweet, and filled with warm spiced apples.
body: Custardy French toast baked with cinnamon-spiced apples until golden-brown for a cozy breakfast that tastes like apple pie.

As they bake, the apples become tender and their juices add a delicious caramel-like sweetness to every bite. To finish it off, make a quick brown sugar whipped cream that’s light, fluffy, and just sweet enough to complement the warm apples. It’s definitely my favorite part, and my kids agree! Whether you’re hosting a holiday brunch, feeding a crowd, or simply looking for something delicious to make on a slow Sunday morning, this French toast is guaranteed to make breakfast feel a little more special. Serve it warm with a dusting of powdered sugar and a generous spoonful of whipped cream (trust me). A drizzle of maple syrup never hurts, either.

As a professionally trained baker and recipe developer with over a decade of experience in food media, I know a thing or two about creating a delicious breakfast. As a working mom of two, I especially love recipes that can be prepared ahead of time and make a busy morning a little more special.

articles.title: Kim Kardashian and Kris Jenner Have Very Different Takes on Sparkle Season
articles.summary: In Rome, mother-daughter duo Kim Kardashian and Kris Jenner had two very different approaches to party-season dressing care of custom Erdem and Chanel.
body: As the days get colder and shorter, one thing to get excited about is that sparkle season is upon us. Longer nights, glitzier parties. But Kim Kardashian and Kris Jenner are evidently working from very different mood boards. The mother-daughter duo, both well-versed in the art of high-impact dressing, stepped out in Rome this week for a night at the Bulgari Hotel, where they attended a reunion party for the cast of All’s Fair. And while both embraced the glittering possibilities of party-season dressing, their respective interpretations couldn’t have been more different.

For Kardashian, the evening called for something rather theatrical. She wore a bespoke Erdem spring 2027 creation, a collaged dress in black and pink crushed satin, with dramatic cutouts, a sheer lace skirt, and suspended crystal flower embellishments that appeared to float across the body. It was a distinctly Kim Kardashian take on eveningwear, thanks to those daringly placed slivers of skin, diaphanous fabrications, and ultra-luxe ornamentation. Kim has never been one to shy away from a complicated silhouette, particularly when it comes to the interplay between the barely-there and the extravagantly embellished.
points: In Rome, mother-daughter duo Kim Kardashian and Kris Jenner had two very different approaches to party-season dressing care of custom Erdem and Chanel.

articles.title: Beauty Marks: The Best Beauty Looks of the Week
articles.summary: From meticulously styled bobs to disco-worthy curls and electric washes of color, this week’s best beauty looks made room for both restraint and revelry.
body: Welcome back to Beauty Marks: Vogue ’s weekly edition of the best moments in celebrity beauty, from Vogue editors’ IG feeds, and all the glam of the fashion and pop culture landscapes. Each week, we curate the nail art to pin for your next nail appointment, new recruits to ‘Team Bob’, and major red carpet moments from the week’s most glamorous affairs. As always, it’s as much about celebrity beauty as it is about the makeup artists, hairstylists, and nail artists, as well as the creators crafting the trends you’re about to see everywhere.

This week in beauty, it was a tale of two extremes. On one hand, there was a return to the classics: immaculate bobs, neat ponytails, and refined, barely-there makeup moments. On the other, a decidedly more-is-more approach took hold, with technicolor eyes, supersized curls, and lips painted every shade from chocolate brown to crimson red. Kerry Washington and Gemma Chan made the case for understated elegance, while Lauryn Hill and True Whitaker embraced a more experimental streak. Elsewhere, Dua Lipa, Alexa Demie, and Nara Smith found their own sweet spots between the two.
points: From meticulously styled bobs to disco-worthy curls and electric washes of color, this week’s best beauty looks made room for both restraint and revelry.

articles.title: In Lofoten, Norway, a Table Is Set Between Peaks and Fjords
articles.summary: Writer Arati Menon heads to Kitchen on the Edge of the World, a four-day event where top chefs harness the Arctic elements and local ingredients to create extraordinary culinary experiences.
body: “Now you know what it’s like to be in the eye of a storm,” said our hiking guide, Audun Rasmussen, with a grin.

I tried to nod, but the wind whipped it into a wobble. We were nearly 2,000 feet up a steep, multi-edged mountain face, and simultaneously getting pelted by rain. If views over picturesque towns and freshwater lakes below are what is typically promised in this part of Northern Norway, today there’d be none. Instead, fog clung to every nook and crevice of the glacial hulks surrounding us.

There was a sense of achievement, certainly. Rain had turned much of our trails into sinking mud, and rock faces to gripless stone. We had used our hands to push past birch and skidded on moss. And we would still have to make our way back down. But for now, we were in the clouds, hiding under rocky overhangs and finding reprieve in reindeer-meat sandwiches, dry fish bites, and chocolate-covered wafers called Kvikk Lunsj that translates to “a quick lunch."
points: Writer Arati Menon heads to Kitchen on the Edge of the World, a four-day event where top chefs harness the Arctic elements and local ingredients to create extraordinary culinary experiences.

articles.title: The Absolute Best Way to Make Pot Roast (I Tested 4 Methods)
articles.summary: Julia Child is always right. READ MORE...
body: Pot roast is a dish that’s meant to be easy, economical, and delicious. This classic comfort-food dish takes a tough cut of beef, usually chuck roast, and slowly braises it with liquid, herbs, and vegetables until the meat is fork-tender and the whole dish is rich, savory, and deeply comforting. It requires more patience than active cooking time, which is part of what makes it so appealing.

Time and again, Julia Child proves she knows a thing or two about making delicious food. In our last pot roast showdown, her overnight wine marinade won against Ina’s recipe. When we tested that technique again here, but this time in our tried-and-true classic pot roast recipe, it once again produced the favorite pot roast of the bunch. Two other versions, though, were close contenders.
